newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - H.K. Newspaper headlines - Oct 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - H.K. Newspaper headlines - Oct 3.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their veracity.
-- ALL MEDIA - Governor Chris Patten gave his last annual policy address ahead of the handover next year.

-- MING PAO DAILY NEWS - Members of the China-picked Preparatory Committee accused Governor Chris Patten of trying to divide Hong Kong people by saying some had lobbied Beijing for their own personal benefit.
-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES - The Governor promised unqualified assistance to the future Chief Executive-designate
-- WEN WEI PO - In the last policy address of the British government during its colonial rule, Chris Patten disseminated pessimistic sentiment and sang the praises of British rule.
-- Deputy director of the New China News Agency Zhang Junsheng said that Patten was being unfriendly to Hong Kong people by saying some of them were lobbying Beijing for their own benefit.
-- ORIENTAL DAILY NEWS - Demonstrators planning to sail to the Diaoyu Islands underwent training at Stanley Beach in preparation for their plans to stage a landing on one of the islets on Oct 6.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST - Chinese President Jiang Zemin had said that the pro-Diaoyu movement in Hong Kong must not affect the territory's peaceful transition to Chinese rule.
-- Jardine Fleming Investment Management has lost the contract to manage $1.00 billion of the Hong Kong Jockey Club's HK$1.8 billion pension fund.
-- China bought one quarter of all US Treasury bonds sold to foreign central banks during the first half of the year.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Shipping tycoon Tung Chee-hwa has reservations about standing for the post of chief executive.
-- Sun Hung Kai Properties announced a 6.52 per cent rise in net profit to $11.04 billion for the year ended 30 June.
